sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, role, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, password_hash | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email: unique lookup for login (findCredentialsByEmail) and duplicate-email check; employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; manager_id: GET /leaves MANAGER scoping resolves direct reports by manager_id

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date, end_date, requested_days, reason, status, approver_id, approval_comment, submitted_at, decided_at, cancelled_by, cancelled_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code; approver_id -> employees.id; cancelled_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: GET /leaves scopes by requester (EMPLOYEE own, MANAGER direct reports); status: status filter on GET /leaves; (employee_id, status): combined visibility + status filter access pattern; (leave_type_code, start_date): date-range + type filtering on list endpoint

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end, entitled_days, used_days, pending_days | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code | indexes: (employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end): unique key for findByKey lookup used by GET /balances/me; employee_id: balance lookup by employee
data_notes: Persistence slice for authentication + read endpoints. Only one schema change: add nullable `password_hash` (text) to `employees` — bcrypt hash, never returned in any response body. All other tables (leave_requests, leave_balances) already exist and are referenced by name; their specs are restated here for the read-path access patterns (visibility scoping, status/date filtering, balance key lookup). No new repository interfaces are required: the existing IEmployeeRepository (PgEmployeeRepository), ILeaveRepository (PgLeaveRequestRepository), and IBalanceRepository (PgLeaveBalanceRepository) already back the read surface. IEmployeeRepository gains one method `findCredentialsByEmail(email)` returning the employee row including password_hash for login verification (hash compared in the auth service, never serialized). Login is a read + token mint (no DB write); all read endpoints are read-only, so no transaction contract is needed.
transaction_contract: EMPTY — this feature is read-only (login performs a credential read + in-memory bcrypt compare + JWT mint; GET endpoints perform reads only). No multi-step writes exist, so no unit-of-work contract is introduced.
